target_customer: Enterprises needing database and infrastructure access control, now AI agent governance
problem: Teams need secure, audited access to databases and systems; later, to run AI agents with centralized access control.
business_model: B2B enterprise software, later usage-based pricing for the AI platform
product_category: Access control and audit platform, AI agent platform

founders.name: Benjamin Yang
education: Hanshin University, bachelor's in computer science
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the only founder; about 15 years developing IDE databases.

founders.name: Brant Hwang
founders.background_notes: Named CEO in the 2021 seed release and author of the YC launch post; not listed as founder on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Proxying and auditing access across many database types with fine-grained policy is standard but demanding enterprise engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integration into access workflows and audit trails creates stickiness, but a field of access management vendors exists.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; company stayed independent and moved toward AI agent governance by 2025.

market_need_then: Chequer's 2019 post described adding access limits and SQL history tracking beyond normal IDE features, reflecting demand for security and audit in database use; no quantified 2020 demand found.

branding.name_origin: CEO Medium post (2019) says many candidates like CakeDB, Cakery, Querify and QueryPy were considered before QueryPie was chosen; meaning not stated.

identity.logo: created in early 2019 with color theme and graphics per designer post

branding.community_and_virality: No community or merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Playful memorable product name chosen deliberately from hundreds, with a design write-up; no evidence of virality.

pivots.to: Enterprise AI agent platform (QueryPie AIP) on MCP
pivots.why: Site says it evolved from data protection into AI agents with centralized governance; exact date from site product launches in 2025 and 2026.

outcome_analysis: QueryPie, run as CHEQUER in Seoul, raised a $17.75M seed in December 2021 and strategic rounds in 2024 from Salesforce Ventures, Z Venture Capital and Shinhan, then repositioned toward AI agent governance. It has about 70 staff on the YC page and shows no shutdown or sale in sources.
notes: Founding year conflicts: YC page and launch post say 2017, company site says 2016, Capterra 2018; YC value used.
